hardware: Cell Broadband Engine CPU, made with Toshiba and IBM: one 3.2 GHz PowerPC core and seven SPE co-processors, six of them for games
Nvidia RSX "Reality Synthesizer" graphics; 256 MB of XDR system memory plus 256 MB of GDDR3 video memory
A Blu-ray drive that also plays DVDs and CDs; games came on Blu-ray discs
A hard drive in every model (20 GB at launch, up to 500 GB later), which owners can replace
HDMI output up to 1080p; wireless Bluetooth controllers (the motion-sensing Sixaxis at launch, the DualShock 3 with vibration from late 2007)
Three designs: the original (2006), the Slim (2009) and the Super Slim (2012)
profile.story:
The PS3 launched at US$499 and US$599, far above the Xbox 360 and the Wii, with a Cell processor developers found hard to program and a thin launch lineup. Sony sold every console at a loss (analysts estimated more than US$240 each at launch), its games division lost about US$1.9 billion in the year after launch, and with the Xbox 360's year-long head start and the cheaper Wii's motion controls, it started a distant third.

It recovered. The Slim of 2009 cut production costs by about 70% and the price to US$299, Blu-ray won the high-definition disc war against HD DVD, the free PlayStation Network grew, and a run of acclaimed games, many of them exclusives (Metal Gear Solid 4, Uncharted 2, Demon's Souls, The Last of Us), built its reputation. It finished with about 87.4 million consoles sold, narrowly ahead of the Xbox 360, and nearly a billion games sold by 2019.
firsts: The first console to use Blu-ray discs for its games
The first console with an HDMI port
The first console to output games at 1080p (Full HD)
Launched with the free PlayStation Network for online play and the PlayStation Store; PlayStation Plus began on it in 2010
profile.endOfLife: The PlayStation 4 replaced it in November 2013. Shipments ended in Europe in March 2016 and in North America in October 2016; the last consoles were made for Japan, until May 29, 2017.

startHere.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
startHere.why: Hideo Kojima's PS3-only finale to Solid Snake's story was one of the main reasons to buy the console in 2008.

startHere.title: Demon's Souls
startHere.why: FromSoftware's demanding action RPG started the Souls series and a whole genre of 'Soulslikes'.

startHere.title: LittleBigPlanet
startHere.why: Its "Play, Create, Share" idea turned players into level designers, and they shared millions of levels.

startHere.title: Journey
startHere.why: A wordless online pilgrimage that showed what small PlayStation Network games could be; its score was the first from a video game nominated for a Grammy.

startHere.title: Resistance: Fall of Man
startHere.why: The best-selling launch game in North America, and GameSpot's and IGN's PS3 Game of the Year.

startHere.title: Gran Turismo 5
startHere.why: Polyphony's long-awaited simulation, one of the console's best-selling games.

startHere.title: The Last of Us
startHere.why: Naughty Dog's 2013 survival story, released just before the PS4, is often named among the greatest games ever made.

profile.discontinued: 1998 (Europe), 1999 (North America); the Super Famicom until September 25, 2003 (Japan)
profile.unitsSold: 49.1 million worldwide (23.35 million in the Americas, 17.17 million in Japan)
hardware: Ricoh 5A22 CPU, based on the 16-bit WDC 65C816, at up to 3.58 MHz; 128 KB of work RAM
Graphics with a palette of 32,768 colors (up to 256 on screen) and Mode 7, which rotates and scales a background layer for pseudo-3D
A sound chip designed by Sony's Ken Kutaragi: eight channels of sampled audio with effects such as echo
Cartridges could carry extra chips, such as the Super FX for 3D polygons and the SA-1 co-processor
A controller with four face buttons (adding X and Y) and two shoulder buttons (L and R)
profile.story:
Nintendo came late to the 16-bit race: NEC's PC Engine and Sega's Mega Drive had been out for years, and in North America Sega's aggressive marketing made the Genesis the "cool" console. The Super NES answered with richer color and sound, Mode 7 effects and the first home version of Street Fighter II, and Nintendo kept key third-party publishers such as Capcom, Konami, Square and Enix. The console war with Sega stayed close for years.

Late hits such as Donkey Kong Country (1994), whose pre-rendered graphics rivaled the new 32-bit consoles, kept it selling after the PlayStation and Saturn arrived. It sold 49.1 million consoles, the most of its generation, and it is regularly ranked among the greatest consoles, largely for its library.
firsts: Mode 7: rotating and scaling backgrounds for pseudo-3D racing and flying (F-Zero, Pilotwings, Super Mario Kart)
Enhancement chips in the cartridge, beginning with the Super FX for Star Fox's 3D polygons in 1993
Shoulder buttons (L and R) on its controller, a layout later controllers kept
Its censored Mortal Kombat, outsold nearly three to one by the uncensored Genesis version, came amid the 1993 US hearings on violent games that led to the ESRB age ratings
profile.endOfLife: The Nintendo 64 followed in 1996. A smaller redesign came in 1997 (US$99 in North America); Nintendo stopped making the console in North America in 1999 and the Super Famicom on September 25, 2003, and new Super Famicom games came out until 2000. Its games live on through the Virtual Console, the Super NES Classic Edition (2017) and Nintendo Switch Online.

startHere.title: Super Mario World
startHere.why: The launch game packed with the console, and its best seller: Yoshi, secret exits and a world map to explore.

startHere.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
startHere.why: The top-down Zelda with a Light and a Dark World, the pattern for most Zelda games since.

startHere.title: Super Metroid
startHere.why: Atmosphere, hidden paths and backtracking that defined the exploration games now called 'Metroidvanias'.

startHere.title: Chrono Trigger
startHere.why: Square's time-travel RPG from a "Dream Team" of Final Fantasy's, Dragon Quest's and Dragon Ball's creators, with many endings.

startHere.title: Final Fantasy VI
startHere.why: Released in North America as Final Fantasy III: a large ensemble story that showed how far 16-bit storytelling could go.

startHere.title: Super Mario Kart
startHere.why: The first Mario Kart, a showcase for Mode 7 that started the kart racing genre.

startHere.title: Street Fighter II Turbo
startHere.why: The SNES got the first home versions of Capcom's arcade phenomenon, a coup in the console war; Turbo is the faster edition.

startHere.title: Donkey Kong Country
startHere.why: Rare's pre-rendered 3D graphics kept the SNES competitive with the new 32-bit consoles.

startHere.title: Star Fox
startHere.why: A chip in the cartridge, the Super FX, drew 3D polygons years before the Nintendo 64.

games.title: The Last of Us
games.text: Naughty Dog's 2013 survival story, released months before the PS4, swept that year's Game of the Year awards and is often named among the greatest games ever made.

games.title: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
games.text: Naughty Dog's blockbuster set a new standard for cinematic action games, weaving set pieces into the play, and won many 2009 Game of the Year awards.

games.title: Red Dead Redemption
games.text: Rockstar's open-world Western, set as the frontier fades in 1911, is one of the most celebrated stories and worlds of its generation.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto IV
games.text: Rockstar's first HD Grand Theft Auto, a grittier Liberty City with physics-driven action, broke entertainment sales records at its 2008 launch.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
games.text: Hideo Kojima's PS3-only finale to Solid Snake's saga, with long cinematic scenes on a dual-layer Blu-ray disc: one of the main reasons to buy the console in 2008.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto V
games.text: Rockstar's three-hero crime epic was the PS3's best-selling game (about 29.5 million copies on it) and went on to become one of the best-selling games ever.

games.title: Demon's Souls
games.text: FromSoftware's demanding action RPG, with players' messages and bloodstains appearing in each other's worlds, started the Souls series and the 'Soulslike' genre.

games.title: BioShock
games.text: The underwater city of Rapture and its twist on player choice made it a landmark of storytelling in shooters; the PS3 version came in 2008, a year after Xbox 360 and PC.

games.title: Batman: Arkham City
games.text: Rocksteady's sequel opened Batman's world into a walled-off super-prison and refined the 'freeflow' combat that many action games copied.

games.title: Portal 2
games.text: Valve's puzzle sequel, with a two-player co-op campaign, came to PS3 with Steamworks and play with PC owners, after Gabe Newell had called the PS3 'a total disaster'.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
games.text: Bethesda's open-world fantasy RPG became one of the best-selling games ever; the PS3 version slowed down as save files grew until patches helped.

games.title: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception
games.text: The third Uncharted brought bigger set pieces (a burning château, a capsizing ship, the desert) and more online play.

games.title: Journey
games.text: Thatgamecompany's wordless desert pilgrimage, where strangers meet online without speaking, won Game of the Year awards; its score was the first from a video game nominated for a Grammy.

games.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
games.text: Rocksteady's 2009 game proved a licensed superhero game could be great, with 'freeflow' combat and detective tools that later games borrowed.

games.title: LittleBigPlanet
games.text: Media Molecule's "Play, Create, Share" platformer turned players into level designers; they made and shared millions of levels.

games.title: Dark Souls
games.text: The spiritual successor to Demon's Souls, with an interlocking world and cryptic lore, made FromSoftware's style famous worldwide.

games.title: Mass Effect 2
games.text: BioWare's space RPG, praised as one of the best of its generation, came to PS3 in 2011 with an interactive comic to stand in for the first game, which PS3 never had.

games.title: The Orange Box
games.text: Five Valve games on one disc: Half-Life 2 and its two episodes, Portal (whose GLaDOS became an icon) and Team Fortress 2.

games.title: BioShock Infinite
games.text: Irrational's floating city of Columbia, and Elizabeth at the player's side, made for one of 2013's most discussed stories.

games.title: Persona 5
games.text: One of the last big PS3 games (2016 in Japan, 2017 worldwide, alongside a PS4 version): Atlus's stylish high-school RPG brought the series to a mainstream audience.

games.title: Rock Band 3
games.text: Harmonix added keyboards and a Pro mode with real notes on real instruments, the height of the plastic-instrument craze.

games.title: God of War III
games.text: Kratos's PS3 debut and the end of his Greek saga, famous for the enormous scale of its battles.

games.title: Fallout 3
games.text: Bethesda took Fallout into first-person 3D in the ruins of Washington, D.C., reviving the series for a new generation.

games.title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare
games.text: Moving the series to modern times, it redefined online shooters with perks, killstreaks and unlockable progression, copied across the genre.

games.title: Street Fighter IV
games.text: The first new main Street Fighter in eleven years revived fighting games worldwide.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
games.text: Kojima's last Metal Gear at Konami, an open-world stealth game, still came to PS3 in 2015, two years into the PS4's life.

games.title: LittleBigPlanet 2
games.text: Sold as a 'platform for games': its tools could build whole games, not just levels, and most of the first game's 3 million-plus levels carried over.

games.title: Rayman Legends
games.text: Ubisoft's hand-drawn platformer, with its celebrated music levels, is one of the best 2D platformers of its time.

games.title: Rayman Origins
games.text: The first game on Ubisoft's UbiArt Framework brought Rayman back to hand-drawn 2D with four-player co-op.

games.title: Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch
games.text: Level-5 made it with Studio Ghibli, whose animation and a Joe Hisaishi score give it the feel of a playable Ghibli film.

games.title: Mass Effect 3
games.text: The end of Commander Shepard's trilogy; its ending caused such an outcry that BioWare released an Extended Cut.

games.title: Killzone 2
games.text: Guerrilla's heavy, gritty shooter was held up against the famous 2005 'target render' trailer, and became a technical showpiece for the PS3.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time
games.text: Often called the best of Insomniac's Future saga, adding time-bending puzzles to the series' weapons and humor.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction
games.text: The series' first PS3 game looked like a playable animated film and was among the first PS3 games to support DualShock 3 vibration.

games.title: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune
games.text: Naughty Dog's first PS3 game introduced Nathan Drake and the cinematic action-adventure the PlayStation studios became known for.

games.title: inFamous 2
games.text: Sucker Punch's superpowered sequel moved to a city inspired by New Orleans, with good and evil choices shaping Cole's powers.

games.title: inFamous
games.text: Sucker Punch's open-world superhero game, where every power is electricity and choices make Cole a hero or infamous.

games.title: Heavy Rain
games.text: Quantic Dream's interactive crime drama, where any of its four leads can die and the story carries on, was a landmark for choice-driven games.

games.title: Dark Souls II
games.text: The first Souls game not directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki built a new kingdom, Drangleic, and a harsher penalty for dying.

games.title: Borderlands 2
games.text: Gearbox's loot-driven co-op shooter, with Handsome Jack as its celebrated villain.

games.title: Burnout Paradise
games.text: Criterion made Burnout an open world, Paradise City, where races start at any intersection, and kept adding to it with free updates.

games.title: Gran Turismo 5
games.text: Polyphony's long-awaited simulation, with over a thousand cars and car damage, was one of the PS3's best-selling games.

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
games.text: The 2009 sequel broke entertainment launch records, earning about US$550 million in its first five days.

games.title: Assassin's Creed II
games.text: Ezio's Renaissance Italy fixed the first game's repetition and made Assassin's Creed one of Ubisoft's biggest series.

games.title: Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood
games.text: Ezio's second chapter, set in Rome, added recruitable assassins and the series' first multiplayer.

games.title: Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag
games.text: A pirate adventure in the Caribbean with ship battles and open-sea exploration, often called one of the best in the series.

games.title: Flower
games.text: Thatgamecompany's game about the wind carrying petals, played by tilting the controller, was an early case for games as art on the PlayStation Network.

games.title: Dead Space 2
games.text: Visceral's sequel moved Isaac Clarke to a space-station city, the Sprawl, adding set pieces and his own trauma to the horror.

games.title: Dead Space
games.text: Survival horror aboard the USG Ishimura, with no on-screen display (health is on Isaac's back) and 'strategic dismemberment', influential for years.

games.title: Resistance: Fall of Man
games.text: The PS3's best-selling launch game in North America, and GameSpot's and IGN's PS3 Game of the Year.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles
games.text: Sega's tactics game with a watercolor look, where each turn moves soldiers in real time, became a cult classic and a series.

games.title: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
games.text: PlatinumGames turned Raiden's spin-off into precise, over-the-top action where the player can cut enemies apart at any angle.

games.title: Bayonetta
games.text: Hideki Kamiya's stylish action game from PlatinumGames; its PS3 port was weaker than the Xbox 360 version.

games.title: Vanquish
games.text: Shinji Mikami's high-speed shooter, with rocket-powered slides, pushed cover shooters toward speed.

games.title: Fallout: New Vegas
games.text: Obsidian's Mojave follow-up to Fallout 3, prized for its writing and factions despite bugs at launch.

games.title: Deus Ex: Human Revolution
games.text: Eidos-Montréal revived the cyberpunk classic, with stealth, hacking and talking as routes to each goal.

games.title: Dishonored
games.text: Arkane's stealth game in plague-ridden Dunwall, with powers such as Blink, rewarded creative play and runs without killing.

games.title: Far Cry 3
games.text: Its open island, outposts to take and villain Vaas set the template for later Far Cry and Ubisoft open worlds.

games.title: Tomb Raider
games.text: Crystal Dynamics' 2013 reboot retold Lara Croft's origin as a survival story and began a new trilogy.

games.title: Mortal Kombat
games.text: NetherRealm's 2011 reboot returned to 2D fighting and retold the first three games; its story mode set a standard for fighting games.

games.title: Tekken Tag Tournament 2
games.text: Namco's tag-team Tekken with almost every character in the series' history.

games.title: Soulcalibur IV
games.text: Namco's weapon fighter, famous for its Star Wars guests: Darth Vader on PS3, Yoda on Xbox 360.

games.title: Wipeout HD
games.text: Studio Liverpool's anti-gravity racer ran at 1080p and 60 frames per second, a PlayStation Network showcase; a boxed version with the Fury expansion came out in Europe.

games.title: Super Stardust HD
games.text: Housemarque's twin-stick shooter was one of the first must-have PlayStation Network games (2007).

games.title: Braid
games.text: Jonathan Blow's time-rewinding puzzle platformer helped start the indie game boom; it came to PS3 in 2009.

games.title: Limbo
games.text: Playdead's eerie black-and-white puzzle platformer is an indie landmark; it came to PS3 in 2011.

games.title: The Walking Dead
games.text: Telltale's choice-driven episodes about Lee and Clementine won many 2012 Game of the Year awards and revived adventure games.

games.title: Battlefield: Bad Company 2
games.text: DICE's shooter where buildings crumble under fire, with a campaign full of humor.

games.title: Battlefield 3
games.text: DICE's modern military shooter on its Frostbite 2 engine, Call of Duty's biggest challenger in 2011.

games.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops
games.text: Treyarch's Cold War story of numbers and conspiracies, with a Zombies mode that became a phenomenon.

games.title: Borderlands
games.text: Gearbox's 2009 'role-playing shooter', with cel-shaded art and procedurally generated guns, started the looter-shooter genre.

games.title: Dragon Age: Origins
games.text: BioWare's dark fantasy RPG, a spiritual successor to Baldur's Gate, with an origin story for each race and class.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
games.text: Bethesda's huge open-world RPG reached PS3 in 2007, a year after Xbox 360 and PC, and set the template for Skyrim.

games.title: Mirror's Edge
games.text: DICE's first-person parkour game, with its striking white city, is a cult favorite for how it moves.

games.title: Devil May Cry 4
games.text: Capcom's stylish action series' first game beyond PlayStation introduced Nero alongside Dante.

games.title: DmC: Devil May Cry
games.text: Ninja Theory's reboot reimagined Dante; its combat was praised even as the redesign divided fans.

games.title: Resident Evil 5
games.text: The series' first HD main game, built around two-player co-op in West Africa, and one of its best sellers.

games.title: Catherine
games.text: Atlus's puzzle game about relationships and nightmares, from the Persona team.

games.title: Yakuza 4
games.text: Sega's crime drama in Kamurocho with four playable heroes, mixing melodrama with the series' side stories.

games.title: Yakuza 3
games.text: Kiryu's first main-series game on PS3, which moved part of the story to Okinawa.

games.title: Tales of Xillia
games.text: The 13th main Tales game, with two heroes, Jude and Milla, whose routes through the story differ.

games.title: Final Fantasy XIII
games.text: Square Enix's first HD Final Fantasy, with fast Paradigm battles; its linear design divided fans, but it sold millions and had two sequels.

games.title: Gran Turismo 6
games.text: The series' last PS3 game, released weeks after the PS4, with more cars and tracks and a tribute to Ayrton Senna.

games.title: MotorStorm
games.text: Evolution Studios' off-road racer, a European launch game and one of the PS3's two biggest games of 2007.

games.title: Killzone 3
games.text: The first Killzone in stereoscopic 3D and with PlayStation Move aiming.

games.title: Resistance 2
games.text: Insomniac's sequel took the war to the United States, with eight-player co-op and 60-player online battles.

games.title: Rock Band 2
games.text: Harmonix's sequel kept the band together: songs from the first game and a growing download store carried over.

games.title: Max Payne 3
games.text: Rockstar's bullet-time shooter moved Max to São Paulo, with a grim story and detailed animation.

games.title: Sleeping Dogs
games.text: An open-world Hong Kong crime story built from the cancelled True Crime: Hong Kong, praised for its martial-arts combat.

games.title: L.A. Noire
games.text: Team Bondi's 1940s detective game captured actors' faces (MotorScan) so players could read suspects during interrogations.

games.title: Just Cause 2
games.text: Avalanche's playground of explosions and grappling-hook stunts over a huge island, Panau.

games.title: Red Faction: Guerrilla
games.text: Volition's Mars uprising, where whole buildings can be brought down (the Geo-Mod 2.0 engine).

games.title: Castle Crashers
games.text: The Behemoth's hand-drawn four-player brawler, an Xbox Live Arcade hit that came to PS3 in 2010.

games.title: Spelunky
games.text: Derek Yu's procedurally generated cave platformer, a landmark of the roguelike revival; it came to PS3 in 2013.

games.title: Guacamelee!
games.text: DrinkBox's Metroidvania steeped in Mexican culture and lucha libre, on PS3 and Vita with one purchase for both.

games.title: Sound Shapes
games.text: A platformer where everything collected adds a note to the level's song, with music by Beck and deadmau5 among others.

games.title: Puppeteer
games.text: Sony Japan's theatrical platformer, played out on a puppet-show stage, where Kutaro fights with magic scissors.

games.title: Tokyo Jungle
games.text: Survive as animals, from Pomeranians to lions, in a Tokyo empty of people: a strange cult favorite from Sony Japan.

games.title: Dragon's Crown
games.text: Vanillaware's hand-painted fantasy brawler with loot and four-player co-op, directed by George Kamitani.

games.title: Skate 3
games.text: EA Black Box's skateboarding game with 'flick-it' stick controls, still loved (and a viral hit for its physics glitches).

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
games.text: The third Zelda brought the top-down adventure to 16 bits with a Light World and a Dark World to cross between, the pattern for most Zelda games since.

games.title: Super Metroid
games.text: Samus's third adventure, all atmosphere and hidden paths, defined the exploration style now called 'Metroidvania' and is a speedrunning favorite.

games.title: Chrono Trigger
games.text: Square's time-travel RPG from a 'Dream Team' (Hironobu Sakaguchi, Yuji Horii and Akira Toriyama), with many endings and a New Game+ that later games copied.

games.title: Super Mario World
games.text: The launch game packed with the console introduced Yoshi and secret exits on a world map; about 20.6 million copies made it the SNES's best seller.

games.title: Final Fantasy VI
games.text: Released in North America as Final Fantasy III: a large ensemble cast, an opera scene, and a villain, Kefka, who ruins the world halfway through; the last main Final Fantasy in 2D.

games.title: Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars
games.text: Square and Nintendo made the first Mario RPG; its timed button presses in battle carried on in Paper Mario and Mario & Luigi.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest
games.text: Rare's sequel starred Diddy and Dixie Kong in pirate-themed worlds, with a celebrated score by David Wise.

games.title: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island
games.text: Yoshi carries baby Mario through a crayon-drawn world; the Super FX 2 chip in the cartridge powers its effects.

games.title: EarthBound
games.text: Shigesato Itoi's funny, strange modern-day RPG sold poorly in North America at first, then became one of the most beloved cult classics.

games.title: Super Mario Kart
games.text: The first Mario Kart started the kart racing genre; Mode 7 tracks and its battle mode made it the fourth best-selling SNES game (8.76 million).

games.title: Street Fighter II Turbo
games.text: The faster "Hyper Fighting" edition of the arcade phenomenon; the SNES had the first home versions of Street Fighter II, a big win in the console war.

games.title: Secret of Mana
games.text: Square's action RPG with real-time battles for up to three players (with a Multitap), and a much-loved score by Hiroki Kikuta.

games.title: Super Castlevania IV
games.text: Konami remade Simon Belmont's quest for 16 bits, with a whip that swings in eight directions and rotating Mode 7 rooms.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country
games.text: Rare's pre-rendered 3D graphics made the SNES look like the new 32-bit consoles; 6.1 million copies sold in its first 45 days, a record at the time.

games.title: Mega Man X
games.text: Capcom's reinvention of Mega Man for a darker future: wall jumps, dashes and armor upgrades.

games.title: Super Punch-Out!!
games.text: Nintendo's boxing game about reading each opponent's tells, with big, colorful fighters.

games.title: Contra III: The Alien Wars
games.text: Konami's run-and-gun with huge bosses and top-down Mode 7 stages; in Europe it became Super Probotector, with robots.

games.title: Final Fantasy IV
games.text: Released in North America as Final Fantasy II: it introduced the Active Time Battle system and a character-driven story, both series staples.

games.title: Star Fox
games.text: The first game with the Super FX chip in its cartridge, drawing 3D polygons years before the Nintendo 64.

games.title: Kirby Super Star
games.text: Several Kirby games in one cartridge, with two-player co-op, including "The Great Cave Offensive" and "Milky Way Wishes".

games.title: Super Street Fighter II
games.text: The edition that added four new fighters: Cammy, Fei Long, T. Hawk and Dee Jay.

games.title: F-Zero
games.text: A Super Famicom launch game: futuristic racing at high speed, a Mode 7 showcase that inspired later racers such as Wipeout.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles IV: Turtles in Time
games.text: Konami's arcade beat 'em up, rebuilt for the SNES with new stages and its famous throw toward the screen.

games.title: Trials of Mana
games.text: Seiken Densetsu 3, in Japanese only until 2019: pick three of six heroes, each with a story of their own.

games.title: Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts
games.text: Capcom's famously hard platformer, where Arthur's armor breaks at one hit; the first in its series made for a home console rather than arcades.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country 3: Dixie Kong's Double Trouble!
games.text: Rare's third Country game, with Dixie and her cousin Kiddy, one of the last big SNES games.

games.title: Final Fantasy V
games.text: Japan-only on the SNES, it perfected the Job system that lets any character learn any class's abilities.

games.title: Terranigma
games.text: Quintet's action RPG about bringing the Earth back to life, released in Japan and Europe but never in North America.

games.title: Illusion of Gaia
games.text: Quintet's action RPG journey through the ruins and wonders of a reimagined Earth.

games.title: Breath of Fire II
games.text: Capcom's dragon-themed RPG sequel, with a darker story and a town that grows as you recruit people.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
games.text: Yasumi Matsuno's tactical RPG of ethnic war and hard choices, a forerunner of Final Fantasy Tactics.

games.title: Harvest Moon
games.text: The first Harvest Moon: farm, befriend a village and marry, a gentle game that started a genre.

games.title: ActRaiser
games.text: Quintet mixed side-scrolling action with god-game city building, early in the console's life.

games.title: Pilotwings
games.text: A Super Famicom launch game: flight lessons in Mode 7 that showed off the console's pseudo-3D.

games.title: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals
games.text: Neverland's RPG, known for its Zelda-like dungeon puzzles and the endless Ancient Cave.

games.title: Demon's Crest
games.text: Capcom's dark adventure starring the gargoyle Firebrand; a commercial failure then, a cult favorite now.

games.title: Mega Man X2
games.text: The second X game used Capcom's Cx4 chip in the cartridge for its wireframe 3D effects.

games.title: Super Mario All-Stars
games.text: The NES Super Mario games remade in 16-bit graphics, including the West's first official release of Japan's harder Super Mario Bros. 2, as The Lost Levels.

games.title: Ogre Battle: The March of the Black Queen
games.text: Yasumi Matsuno's real-time strategy RPG with branching endings, the first Ogre Battle.

games.title: Street Fighter Alpha 2
games.text: A late SNES port that used a compression chip (the S-DD1) to fit the arcade game onto a cartridge.

games.title: Sunset Riders
games.text: Konami's Wild West arcade run-and-gun, brought to the SNES in 1993.

games.title: Killer Instinct
games.text: Rare's fighting game of long combos and pre-rendered fighters; the SNES version came on a black cartridge.

games.title: Zombies Ate My Neighbors
games.text: LucasArts' two-player run-and-gun parody of horror movies: rescue the neighbors from B-movie monsters.

games.title: Dragon Quest V
games.text: A story that follows its hero from childhood to fatherhood, with monsters that join the party; not in English until the 2009 DS remake.

games.title: Fire Emblem: Genealogy of the Holy War
games.text: The fourth Fire Emblem told its story across two generations, with children inheriting their parents' traits.

games.title: Live A Live
games.text: Square's anthology RPG of seven stories across time, in Japanese only until its 2022 remake on Nintendo Switch.

games.title: Secret of Evermore
games.text: Square's only game made in the United States: a boy and his shape-shifting dog in worlds out of B movies.

games.title: Soul Blazer
games.text: Quintet's action RPG, where clearing monster lairs frees the souls of a world's people.

games.title: Kirby's Dream Course
games.text: Kirby as the ball in a mini-golf puzzle game from HAL Laboratory.

games.title: Uniracers
games.text: DMA Design's unicycle stunt racer; a Pixar lawsuit over its unicycle stopped production, so cartridges are scarce.

games.title: Axelay
games.text: Konami's shooter whose vertical stages roll away like a drum, a technical showpiece.

games.title: Super Bomberman 2
games.text: Hudson's party classic for up to four players with a Multitap.

games.title: Mortal Kombat II
games.text: Unlike the first game, the SNES version kept the blood and fatalities, once age ratings had arrived.

games.title: NBA Jam
games.text: Midway's over-the-top two-on-two basketball ("He's on fire!") was a huge arcade and home hit.

games.title: Tetris Attack
games.text: Japan's Panel de Pon, dressed with Yoshi's Island characters for the West: a fast block-swapping puzzler.

games.title: Star Ocean
games.text: tri-Ace's science-fiction RPG squeezed 48 megabits and voice clips onto a cartridge with a compression chip; Japan only until later remakes.

games.title: Romancing SaGa 3
games.text: Square's open-ended RPG with eight heroes to choose from; Japan only until a 2019 remaster.

games.title: Front Mission
games.text: Square's mech tactics RPG of a near-future war; Japan only on the Super Famicom.

games.title: Bahamut Lagoon
games.text: Square's tactics RPG of commanding dragons, a late Super Famicom game never sold in English.

games.title: Dragon Quest VI
games.text: The last of the Zenithian trilogy, with a dream world beside the real one; in English from the 2011 DS remake.

games.title: Dragon Quest III
games.text: A 1996 Super Famicom remake of the classic Famicom RPG, with new graphics and extras; Japan only.

games.title: Rock n' Roll Racing
games.text: Combat racing to licensed rock and metal songs, made by Silicon & Synapse, soon renamed Blizzard Entertainment.

games.title: The Lost Vikings
games.text: Blizzard's early puzzle platformer (as Silicon & Synapse): three Vikings with different skills who must work together.

games.title: Pocky & Rocky
games.text: Natsume's co-op shooter: a shrine maiden and a tanuki against monsters from Japanese folklore.

games.title: The Legend of the Mystical Ninja
games.text: The first Ganbare Goemon game released in the West: a comic adventure through Edo-period Japan.

games.title: Super Turrican 2
games.text: Factor 5's run-and-gun showcase of what the SNES could do with graphics and sound.

games.title: Kirby's Dream Land 3
games.text: Kirby with a crayon look and animal friends, and the last SNES game Nintendo published in North America (1997).

games.title: Mega Man 7
games.text: The original Mega Man's 16-bit entry, which introduced Bass and Treble.

games.title: Mega Man X3
games.text: The last Mega Man X on the SNES, where Zero became playable.

games.title: Breath of Fire
games.text: Capcom's first Breath of Fire, starting the series of Ryu, who turns into dragons.

games.title: Shadowrun
games.text: The cyberpunk tabletop RPG as a noir mystery, driven by keywords learned in conversation.

games.title: Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
games.text: The second of LucasArts' famously hard Super Star Wars games, adding Luke's Force powers.

games.title: Super Star Wars
games.text: LucasArts' side-scrolling take on the 1977 film, known for its difficulty and its X-wing stage.

games.title: Disney's Aladdin
games.text: Capcom's SNES Aladdin, a different game from Virgin's Genesis version, and a polished platformer in its own right.

games.title: The Magical Quest Starring Mickey Mouse
games.text: Capcom's Mickey Mouse platformer, where costumes change his powers.

games.title: SimCity
games.text: Will Wright's city builder, with Nintendo's own touches: Dr. Wright as an adviser and Bowser as a disaster.

games.title: Wild Guns
games.text: Natsume's steampunk Western shooting gallery, a cult favorite for two players.

games.title: The Ninja Warriors
games.text: Natsume's beat 'em up with robot ninjas, released as The Ninja Warriors Again in Japan.

games.title: Earthworm Jim
games.text: Shiny Entertainment's surreal, hand-animated platformer starring a worm in a robot suit.

games.title: Mario Paint
games.text: It came with the SNES Mouse: drawing, animation and a music composer whose songs still circulate online.

games.title: Ken Griffey Jr. Presents Major League Baseball
games.text: Nintendo's baseball game with real teams and stadiums but fictional players; only Griffey himself was real.

games.title: Tecmo Super Bowl
games.text: The SNES follow-up to Tecmo's NES classic, which was the first game licensed by both the NFL and its players' union.

games.title: Super Tennis
games.text: An early SNES sports game with quick, precise tennis, still well regarded.

games.title: International Superstar Soccer Deluxe
games.text: Konami's soccer game, a forerunner of the Pro Evolution Soccer series.

games.title: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3
games.text: The fullest Mortal Kombat 3, bringing back favorites such as Scorpion and Kitana.

games.title: Gradius III
games.text: Konami's arcade shooter, a North American launch game, known for slowing down when the screen got busy.

games.title: R-Type III: The Third Lightning
games.text: Irem's R-Type made for the SNES, with new Force devices.

games.title: Castlevania: Dracula X
games.text: A reworked version of the PC Engine's Rondo of Blood, with new levels.

games.title: Sparkster
games.text: Konami's rocket-powered opossum, the only Rocket Knight game on a Nintendo console.

games.title: Super Adventure Island
games.text: Hudson's platformer with a soundtrack by Yuzo Koshiro.

games.title: Tales of Phantasia
games.text: The first Tales game, on a 48-megabit cartridge that even held an opening song with vocals.

games.title: Fire Emblem: Thracia 776
games.text: The last Super Famicom Fire Emblem (1999), sold first through Nintendo Power download kiosks.

games.title: Wario's Woods
games.text: Toad's puzzle game, also the last game Nintendo released for the NES in North America.

games.title: Plok
games.text: Software Creations' platformer whose hero throws his own limbs, with music by Tim and Geoff Follin.

games.title: Clock Tower
games.text: Human's point-and-click horror game of hiding from the Scissorman; Japan only on the Super Famicom.

games.title: Metal Warriors
games.text: LucasArts' mech action game with two-player versus battles, released only in North America.

games.title: Mega Man & Bass
games.text: A late Super Famicom game (1998) where Bass is playable; in English from the 2003 Game Boy Advance version.

games.title: Flashback
games.text: Delphine's rotoscoped science-fiction adventure, a cinematic platformer in the style of Another World.

games.title: Stunt Race FX
games.text: Nintendo's second Super FX game: 3D racing with cartoon cars.

games.title: Top Gear
games.text: Kemco's split-screen racer with a memorable soundtrack by Barry Leitch.
